_comment: GENERATED by `python3 -m edge_workbench check`. Do not edit:
re-run it. This is what the build reads instead of the
tutorial, so that a build depends on files in this repository
and not on which branch a sibling checkout happens to be on.
`source.sha` is the commit the tutorial was read at. A gate
compares it against the tutorial's head to tell you when the
tutorial has moved and this needs re-running.
`gaps` lists what the tutorial does not state in a form this
step can read. Those are the model-assisted half's input; an
empty list means the tutorial said everything itself.

example.quote: Consider the five-vertex graph with directed edges

meanings.init: The frontier starts with only the source, the source is recorded as its own parent, and the search begins in top-down mode.
meanings.E01: Find the vertices that already have a parent in the BFS tree.
meanings.E02: The Not Visited vertices are the ones with no parent yet.
meanings.E03: Run the top-down macro or the bottom-up macro for this level, whichever the current mode says; either one gives the updated tree, the next frontier and the next mode.
meanings.E04: From all vertices in the frontier, collect all outgoing neighbors.
meanings.E05: Keep only neighbors that have not been discovered before.
meanings.E06: Record every frontier vertex that reaches a newly discovered vertex as a candidate parent.
meanings.E07: If several frontier vertices discover the same child, keep one of them as its parent.
meanings.E08: Add the newly discovered parent-child edges to the BFS tree.
meanings.E09: The next frontier is the set of newly discovered vertices.
meanings.E10: Estimate the work of a top-down step: the number of edges leaving the frontier.
meanings.E11: Estimate the work of a bottom-up step: the number of edges into Not Visited vertices.
meanings.E12: Decide whether the frontier's work has grown past the threshold, so the next level should go bottom-up.
meanings.E13: The next level stays top-down unless the switch condition held.
meanings.E14: For each Not Visited vertex, find all of its potential parents.
meanings.E15: A Not Visited vertex is discovered if at least one of its parents is in the frontier.
meanings.E16: Choose a single parent for each newly discovered vertex.
meanings.E17: Record the newly discovered vertices in the BFS tree.
meanings.E18: The next frontier is the set of vertices that were just discovered.
meanings.E19: Count the vertices in the frontier.
meanings.E20: Decide whether the frontier has become small enough to go back to top-down.
meanings.E21: The next level goes back to top-down only if that check held; otherwise it stays bottom-up.
meanings.stop: The search ends when no new vertices were discovered.

tensorNotes.G: The graph: true where edge s to d exists.
tensorNotes.F: The frontier: the vertices being expanded at this level.
tensorNotes.Tree: The BFS tree: true where s is recorded as the parent of d.
tensorNotes.TopDown: The traversal mode: true when this level runs the top-down macro.
tensorNotes.Visited: Vertices with a parent recorded in the tree.
tensorNotes.NV: Not Visited: vertices with no parent recorded yet.
tensorNotes.NeiNV: Neighbors of the frontier that are Not Visited, the new discoveries (top-down).
tensorNotes.CandTree: Candidate parent-child edges for the new discoveries (top-down).
tensorNotes.CandParents: Edges into Not Visited vertices: their candidate parents (bottom-up).
tensorNotes.InF: Candidate parents that are in the frontier (bottom-up).
tensorNotes.Temp: The one parent selected for each new child.
tensorNotes.MF: Top-down work estimate: edges leaving the frontier.
tensorNotes.MU: Bottom-up work estimate: edges into Not Visited vertices.
tensorNotes.NF: The number of vertices in the frontier.
tensorNotes.TB: True when the next level should switch from top-down to bottom-up.
tensorNotes.BT: True when the next level should switch from bottom-up back to top-down.

quotes.init: The frontier contains only the source, and the source is its own parent
quotes.E01: we first determine which vertices do not yet have parents recorded in the BFS tree
quotes.E03: The selected macro computes three outputs simultaneously: the updated BFS tree, the next frontier, and the traversal mode for the next iteration.
quotes.E04: From all vertices in the frontier, collect all outgoing neighbors.
quotes.E05: Keep only neighbors that have not been discovered before.
quotes.E06: Record all parents for newly discovered vertices from the frontier.
quotes.E07: If multiple frontier vertices discover the same child, keep the first one found as the parent.
quotes.E08: Add the newly discovered parent-child edges into the BFS tree.
quotes.E09: Set the next frontier to all newly discovered vertices.
quotes.E10: the sum of degrees of vertices in the frontier
quotes.E11: the sum of degrees of Not Visited vertices
quotes.E12: we estimate whether the next iteration should remain top-down or switch to bottom-up
quotes.E13: the macro sets the next traversal mode to Bottom-Up
quotes.E14: For each Not Visited vertex, identify all of its potential parents.
quotes.E15: A Not Visited vertex becomes discovered if at least one of its parents is in the frontier.
quotes.E16: Choose a single parent for each newly discovered vertex.
quotes.E17: Record newly discovered vertices in the BFS tree.
quotes.E18: The new frontier contains vertices that were just discovered.
quotes.E20: the algorithm checks whether the frontier has become small enough to switch back to top-down
quotes.E21: the macro sets the next traversal mode to Top-Down
quotes.stop: the hybrid algorithm terminates when the newly computed frontier is empty
